title: Regenerate ACP schema and TypeScript artifacts for the custom-provider ACP DTO
description: crates/goose-sdk-types/src/custom_requests.rs adds CustomAcpConfigDto and the acp field on CustomProviderConfigDto/CustomProviderUpsertDto, but the generated artifacts were not regenerated.
acceptance_criteria: just check-acp-artifacts passes: crates/goose/acp-schema.json, crates/goose/acp-meta.json, and ui/goose-acp-client/src/generated/ match the Rust DTOs, and ui/desktop typechecks against them.
notes:
Evidence: grep CustomAcpConfigDto crates/goose/acp-schema.json returns 0 matches, and the generated CustomProviderCreateRequest_unstable in ui/goose-acp-client/src/generated/types.gen.ts has no acp field, so ui/desktop/src/acp/providers.ts and ProviderGrid.tsx reference a field the generated API type does not declare.

Justfile:154 check-acp-artifacts runs generate-acp-types then git diff --exit-code on those paths, so this currently fails a required gate.

Blocked in this environment: just generate-acp-schema requires the local-inference feature (the checked-in schema contains 84 LocalInference references, so regenerating without it would drop types), which needs libclang for llama-cpp-sys bindgen; the TypeScript step needs node plus @hey-api/openapi-ts via pnpm install. Neither libclang nor pnpm is installed here.
close_reason: Rust schema, TypeScript types, and generated client all regenerated and verified byte-identical on a second run; documentation generator taught to render tuple arrays so the docs build and check-acp-artifacts pass.

comments.author: Daniel Jay Haskin
comments.text:
Artifacts regenerated with the real generators after installing the missing toolchain (dnf clang-devel, llvm-devel, cmake, pnpm 10.33.0).

- just generate-acp-schema equivalent: cargo run --features code-mode,local-inference,aws-providers,telemetry,otel,rustls-tls,system-keyring --bin generate-acp-schema. crates/goose/acp-schema.json gains exactly the ACP additions (+103 lines: acp on the custom-provider DTOs plus CustomAcpConfigDto); acp-meta.json is unchanged because no methods were added.
- TypeScript: ui/goose-acp-client pnpm run generate => generated types.gen.ts/zod.gen.ts/index.ts now carry CustomAcpConfigDto and acp?: CustomAcpConfigDto | null; the package builds (tsc) so ui/desktop can resolve it.
- Idempotency verified: re-running both generators leaves the artifacts byte-identical (md5sum -c OK for schema, meta, and all four generated files), so the check-acp-artifacts diff gate is satisfied.

One extra fix was required. The docs generator (documentation/scripts/generate-acp-docs.js) threw 'Unsupported schema keyword: prefixItems' because Vec<(String, String)> renders as a JSON Schema tuple, and that keyword was blacklisted. It now renders tuples as [string, string], which is how env and sessionConfigOptions appear in the generated reference. Without this, the docs build and the check-acp-artifacts prerequisite would fail for any tuple-shaped field.

comments.author: Daniel Jay Haskin
comments.text:
Controlled stdio fixture landed: crates/goose/tests/fake_acp_agent.py (dependency-free ACP agent that writes a JSON transcript of the traffic and its launch environment) plus crates/goose/tests/generic_acp_stdio_test.rs, which drives the fixture through ProviderRegistry::register_generic_acp -> create so the assertions cover the real launch path, not an in-process transport.

Nine tests, all green (cargo test -p goose --test generic_acp_stdio_test, 9/9):
- argv/env/env_remove/launch interpreter, session cwd from work_dir, MCP stdio forwarding with env shape, structured session config options applied once (redundant-send guard), prompt round trip.
- work_dir unset: the caller-supplied working directory becomes the session cwd.
- mode_mapping: goose's permission mode is translated to the agent mode id; an unmapped mode fails loudly with requested vs available modes.
- failure stages are distinguishable: discovery (could not resolve command), launch (failed to spawn ACP process + OS cause), handshake (ACP initialize failed), downstream auth (ProviderError::Authentication).
- MCP forwarding honours advertised capabilities (http dropped unless advertised).
- session resume moves to the saved session and closes the replaced one.
- provider drop terminates the agent process (heartbeat stops advancing).

Fixture exposed and fixed two gaps: launch errors were re-wrapped as strings and lost the OS cause, and the docs described work_dir as the process directory. Details on .2.2 and .7.

title: Audit generic ACP tests with fresh reviewers
description: Have independent reviewers inspect implementation and tests for tautological assertions, accidental built-in Pi use, missing security coverage, and legacy/state-machine parity gaps.
acceptance_criteria: Review findings are recorded in Beads, addressed in code/tests, and targeted plus required quality gates are green.
notes: Fresh delegated audit task 20260913_2 reached its action limit without returning findings. Local review found no blocking issue in the committed diff. All targeted tests and clippy/typecheck gates pass; generated artifact regeneration is clean. Keep in_progress for an explicit fresh review before closing.

comments.author: Daniel Jay Haskin
comments.text:
Adversarial self-review of the new suite (an independent reviewer is still required before this closes).

Checked and clean:
- No tautological assertions: each one pins externally observable behaviour (the agent's own JSON transcript, provider_session_id, streamed text, error variants/messages). Assertions were falsified during development and failed as expected (argv shape, MCP env shape, launch error detail, mcpServers filtering).
- No accidental built-in use: the Pi-shaped test registers both providers and proves the custom entry runs the configured command, so a silent fallback to pi-acp would fail it.
- No implementation-detail coupling: the only production API added is ProviderRegistry::entry; no private fields are inspected.
- Secret handling: the fixture records only the environment variable names the test explicitly watches, so no secrets are written to the transcript; env_remove is asserted by absence.

Weaknesses to fix or accept:
- Each test skips with an eprintln when no python interpreter exists, which would silently reduce coverage on a runner without python. Consider failing instead, or adding a CI-only assertion that the interpreter is present.
- ACP session/cancel is never issued by goose, so the fixture's cancel path is unexercised dead coverage; either wire a cancellation test or drop the branch.
- Capability filtering is asserted for http only; sse is intentionally never forwarded, and stdio is untested against an agent that advertises stdio=false (v1 treats stdio as mandatory).
- Mode mapping is asserted for one GooseMode value in a config created only through the test helper; the CLI/desktop surfaces never write mode_mapping, so its only path is direct file editing.

comments.author: Daniel Jay Haskin
comments.text:
Desktop verification is now green, and running the typecheck exposed two real bugs that are fixed.

Bugs found by pnpm run typecheck and by reading the form's save payload:
1. ProviderGrid passed acp.args (optional in the generated DTO) into a local type that requires args: string[], and the form calls initialData.acp.args.join(', '). Editing a saved ACP provider whose file omits args would have crashed the form. Now defaults to [].
2. The form never read or sent model_config_option_id and hardcoded session_config_options: []. Editing a provider silently dropped both, which changes runtime behaviour: model_config_option_id drives model selection and session_config_options are applied at session/new. Both are now round-tripped, with model_config_option_id as a text input and session_config_options as a NAME=value editor mirroring the existing environment editor. The duplicated env parsing was folded into parseNameValueLines/formatNameValueLines/parseCommaSeparated helpers.

New tests in CustomProviderForm.test.tsx (3 added, file now 12/12): persisted ACP launch fields load into the form; submitting sends every persisted field including model_config_option_id and session_config_options; an ACP provider without a command is blocked.

Verification: pnpm run typecheck clean; pnpm test --run --testTimeout=30000 src/.../CustomProviderForm.test.tsx 12/12. title: Preserve ACP capabilities across custom-provider sessions
description: Exercise MCP forwarding, initialization negotiation, session creation/resume behavior, prompt streaming, cancellation, permission modes, and model/config option handling through the generic adapter.
acceptance_criteria: Runtime tests cover supported and unsupported capabilities and preserve parity in both legacy and state-machine agent paths where applicable.
close_reason: Runtime coverage through the generic route: initialization negotiation and capability-filtered MCP forwarding, session creation with cwd and MCP servers, session resume with retirement of the replaced session, prompt streaming, model/config options, mode mapping with a loud failure for unmapped modes, and teardown. Remaining gaps (no session/cancel issuer in goose, permission-request and effort mirroring already covered in-process) are recorded on the issue.

comments.author: Daniel Jay Haskin
comments.text:
Capability coverage through the generic route is now behavioural rather than inferential.

Covered by crates/goose/tests/generic_acp_stdio_test.rs:
- Initialization negotiation: the agent's advertised capabilities drive the request (MCP http capability gates http server forwarding; stdio servers always forward and carry the spec env shape {"name","value"}).
- Session creation with cwd and MCP servers, plus session resume: the provider moves to the saved session and closes the session it created during connect.
- Prompt streaming: the agent's agent_message_chunk arrives as goose text and the prompt reaches the agent unchanged.
- Mode mapping: goose's permission mode is translated to the agent's mode id, and an unmapped mode fails with requested vs available modes instead of silently leaving the agent in its own default permission level.
- Model/config option handling: structured session config options are applied at session/new, and the active model is not re-sent when it already matches.
- Cleanup: dropping the provider terminates the agent process.

Known gaps, recorded rather than silently skipped:
- goose never sends session/cancel, so cancellation is 'stop consuming and drop the provider' (which the teardown test covers). The fixture already answers session/cancel with stopReason cancelled if a client ever sends it.
- session/request_permission round trips, terminal delegation, and thinking-effort mirroring are pre-existing AcpProvider behaviours already covered in-process by acp_provider_test/acp_bootstrap_effort_test; the new suite deliberately targets the generic registration and launch route.
- Parity: the generic provider is registered and constructed in the provider registry, which both the legacy and state-machine agent loops consume, and the tests exercise that layer without touching agent-loop code, so no legacy/state-machine delta exists for this change.

Tests: generic_acp_stdio_test 9/9, acp_provider_test 12/12, acp_bootstrap_effort_test 3/3, acp_transport_auth_test 35/35, acp_server_test 57/57.

comments.author: Daniel Jay Haskin
comments.text:
CLI verification is green (the libclang/cmake blockers are gone) and the ACP setup flow was completed and made testable.

Compile/quality gates: cargo clippy -p goose-cli --all-targets -D warnings clean, cargo fmt clean, git diff --check clean, cargo test -p goose-cli --lib 336/336 passed.

Gaps closed in the CLI flow:
1. The ACP branch hardcoded env: [] and env_remove: [], so the CLI could not configure the environment mutations the design requires (and that the desktop already collects). Both are now prompted: comma-separated NAME=value additions and comma-separated removals.
2. model_config_option_id was hardcoded to Some("model"). The design explicitly says model/mode option IDs must be negotiated from the installed agent rather than assumed, and assuming an id makes goose send a model switch at the first prompt. It is now an optional prompt that defaults to unset.

New tests (5, in the existing configure.rs test module): a Kiro command with named-agent arguments keeps its argument vector; environment additions parse NAME=value, bare NAME, and padded values while removals stay ordered; unset optional fields stay empty (including the model option id); explicit work_dir and model option id are recorded and trimmed; an empty command is rejected.

title: Harden ACP subprocess discovery and launch semantics
description: Resolve commands using established search paths, launch exact argv without a shell, apply cwd and environment mutations safely, and preserve subprocess cleanup and error classification.
acceptance_criteria: Controlled launch tests prove argv/environment/cwd behavior and ensure command, launch, handshake, and authentication failures are actionable without secret leakage.

comments.author: Daniel Jay Haskin
comments.text:
Launch semantics are now proven against a real subprocess, and the fixture found one defect that is fixed.

Evidence (crates/goose/tests/generic_acp_stdio_test.rs):
- The configured argv reaches the agent verbatim, including an argument containing 'a b; echo pwned', so no shell interpretation can occur.
- env additions are forwarded and env_remove entries are absent from the agent environment; only the variable names the test explicitly watches are recorded, so no secret material lands in the transcript.
- work_dir becomes the ACP session cwd (absolute); the subprocess inherits goose's cwd, matching the built-in ACP providers.
- Failure classes stay distinct: discovery (could not resolve command 'X': file does not exist), launch (failed to spawn ACP process: <os cause>), handshake (ACP initialize failed), downstream auth (ProviderError::Authentication).

Fix: AcpClientLoop::spawn re-wrapped the spawn error with anyhow!("{e}"), which flattened the chain, so users saw only 'failed to spawn ACP process' with no indication of why (missing vs not executable). The original anyhow error is now forwarded to connect and the log line uses {e:#}.

Verification: cargo fmt, cargo clippy -p goose --all-targets -D warnings, cargo test -p goose --test generic_acp_stdio_test (9/9), acp_provider_test 12/12, acp_custom_provider_methods_test 2/2, goose-providers 220/220, goose lib provider_registry 3/3.

title: Generic custom ACP provider flow for goose
description: Plan and track the end-to-end goose feature that lets users define local stdio ACP agents through the existing Custom provider flow, then select them like saved HTTP custom providers.
design: Follow the proposed design at https://github.com/djha-skin/opensource-work/wiki/Goose-Generic-Custom-ACP-Provider-Design. Do not implement upstream changes until the goose issue/design is maintainer-approved and marked Ready.

title: ACP turns cannot be cancelled: goose never sends session/cancel
description: User interrupts and stream drops never reach the agent: no ACP provider sends session/cancel, so the agent keeps working after goose stops consuming its output.
acceptance_criteria: Interrupting an ACP turn stops the agent's work (or the limitation is documented as intentional and the untestable fixture branch is removed).
notes: The uncommitted runtime changes now implement keyed turn cancellation: dropping an ACP stream signals its exact (session, turn) key, the client loop sends session/cancel while that prompt is in flight, and stale cancellation signals cannot cancel a subsequent turn. The new controlled fixture test abandoned_generic_acp_turn_cancels_the_agent passes. Keep this issue open until the change is reviewed and committed; it is pre-existing behavior shared by built-in ACP providers as well as generic custom ACP.

comments.author: Daniel Jay Haskin
comments.text:
Final documentation pass complete.

- The generic ACP examples and JSON shapes match DeclarativeAcpConfig and the declarative custom-provider schema (same shape the new integration tests deserialize), and the guide keeps the Pi custom example distinct from the built-in pi-acp provider.
- Corrected a claim the runtime does not make: the getting-started table described work_dir as the ACP process directory, while goose (matching the built-in ACP providers) launches the agent in goose's working directory and sends work_dir as the ACP session cwd. The fixture test pins that behaviour, and the ACP guide now says so.
- Added operational caveats for env/env_remove secret handling and for the optional mode_mapping (JSON-only, affects permission behaviour, unknown mode IDs fail at provider start).
